stories.title: Bermuda Championship Starts Thursday — Full Preview

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: The Bermuda Championship starts Thursday at Port Royal. $6M purse, 500 FedExCup points, 120 players. It's the shortest course on Tour at 6,828 yards. Wind turns par 71 into a survival test. Adam Schenk defends. Austin Lemieux debuts. #GolfFanrecap #BermudaChampionship

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: Port Royal has produced a different champion every year since 2019. Schenk, Campos, Villegas, Power, Herbert, Gay, Todd — no repeats. Can Schenk become the first back-to-back winner in Bermuda Championship history? Round 1 Thursday. #GolfFanrecap #PGATour

facebook.long_form:
The PGA Tour heads to Bermuda this week, and Port Royal Golf Course is a different kind of test.

The Butterfield Bermuda Championship runs October 22-25 at Port Royal in Southampton. At 6,828 yards and par 71, it is the shortest layout on the PGA Tour calendar. What makes it hard isn't the distance — it's the wind. Port Royal sits on the water and funnels Atlantic wind through fairways and across greens in ways that can completely change what a hole plays like from one round to the next.

The $6 million purse carries 500 FedExCup points. Adam Schenk won here last year at 12-under par. He's back this week as the defending champion.

The field of 120 also includes Austin Lemieux — son of hockey legend Mario Lemieux — who earned his spot at a Monday qualifier by shooting 66. He'll play as an amateur. The Bermuda Championship has been running since 2019, and it has never had a back-to-back champion. Every edition has produced a different winner.

Round 1 tees off Thursday. Golf Channel has coverage.

stories.title: Jon Rahm LIV Exit — Nov. 5 Hearing Is the Next Step

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: Jon Rahm's separation from LIV is filed. Court hearing is November 5. After approval, he can join any tour or league without asking LIV's permission. NIL rights restored. Abu Dhabi Championship Nov 5-8 is reportedly the target for his return. #GolfFanrecap #JonRahm

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: Rahm told the court LIV 2.0 terms were unacceptable. He walked away from what reports called $100M+ in remaining guarantees. The court decides November 5. The PGA Tour is waiting. So is everyone else. #GolfFanrecap #LIVGolf

facebook.long_form:
Jon Rahm's exit from LIV Golf is now a filed legal document. The next stop is a New Jersey courtroom.

Rahm's separation agreement with LIV was filed in bankruptcy court around October 15. A judge is scheduled to hear the case on November 5. Under the agreement's terms, Rahm is released from all remaining performance obligations — he owes LIV nothing. He can sign with any tour, league, or sponsor without notifying or seeking permission from LIV. His name, image, and likeness rights are returned to him.

Rahm told the court through his attorney that he reviewed the proposed terms of LIV's restructured league and found them unacceptable. He walked away from what some reports estimated as more than $100 million in remaining contract guarantees.

The PGA Tour has said it will not hold conversations with any LIV player still legally under contract. That clock runs through November 5. Rahm is reportedly targeting the Abu Dhabi Championship, which runs November 5-8, as his first event back.

The process is not finished yet. But the path is clear.

stories.title: Chacarra Wins India, Jumps to No. 1 in Race to Dubai

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: Eugenio Chacarra was runner-up in Spain last Sunday. He won in India this Sunday. Back-to-back weeks in contention, two different continents. He's now No. 1 in the Race to Dubai. #GolfFanrecap #DPWorldTour

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: Chacarra wins the DP World India Championship and takes the Race to Dubai lead from Patrick Reed. The $4M event at Delhi Golf Club goes to the hottest player on the European Tour right now. #GolfFanrecap #RaceToDubai

facebook.long_form:
Last Sunday, Eugenio Chacarra was the runner-up at the Open de España. One stroke behind Grant Forrest. So close.

This Sunday, Chacarra won the DP World India Championship at Delhi Golf Club, taking the $4 million event on October 18. Then he took the lead in the Race to Dubai.

That's two weekends, two different countries, two top finishes — with a victory to close the stretch. It's the kind of back-to-back run that turns a strong European Tour season into a great one.

Heading into the India event, Patrick Reed held the Race to Dubai lead by a significant margin. Tommy Fleetwood was the defending champion. Chacarra came in already in strong form and delivered a final round that held up under pressure.

He is the hottest player in European Tour golf right now. With the Race to Dubai heading into its final events, Chacarra is exactly where he wants to be.

stories.title: Adam Schenk Defends at Port Royal — What to Expect

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: Adam Schenk won the 2025 Bermuda Championship at 12-under. He's back at Port Royal this week to defend. No player has won back-to-back at this event in its seven-year history. Schenk has a chance to be the first. #GolfFanrecap #BermudaChampionship

facebook.long_form:
Adam Schenk won the 2025 Butterfield Bermuda Championship at 12-under par. He navigated Port Royal's wind-battered layout, scrambled when he had to, and made the putts that mattered.

Now he comes back as the defending champion.

Defending a title means facing the same course that elevated you, competing against a field that has studied how you won. At Port Royal, the challenge is consistent: the course is the same par-71 layout, the same wind can roll in off the Atlantic, and the same premium on scrambling and putting remains.

The Bermuda Championship has been running since 2019. In seven editions, no player has won it twice. Todd won in 2019. Gay won in 2020. Herbert in 2021, Power in 2022, Villegas in 2023, Campos in 2024, Schenk in 2025. Seven events, seven champions.

Schenk has a chance to become the first back-to-back winner in the tournament's history. Round 1 is Thursday.

stories.title: Austin Lemieux's PGA Tour Debut — Mario's Son Tees It Up in Bermuda

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text: Mario Lemieux's son Austin is making his PGA Tour debut this week. He shot 66 at a Monday qualifier to earn his spot. He plays as an amateur. He's won the 2026 WPGA Mid-Am. He's 23 years old. Port Royal, Thursday. #GolfFanrecap #BermudaChampionship

facebook.long_form:
Mario Lemieux is one of the greatest hockey players who ever lived — two Stanley Cups, the 1992 Conn Smythe Trophy, the Hall of Fame. His son Austin grew up in that shadow.

Austin Lemieux played hockey too. He suited up in the USHL and spent two seasons at Arizona State. He never signed an NHL contract, and he retired from the sport in 2020.

Then he picked up golf.

This week, Austin Lemieux will make his PGA Tour debut at the Butterfield Bermuda Championship, starting Thursday. He earned his entry at a Monday qualifier in Winter Haven, Florida, where he shot 66 — good enough for tied second among 68 players and one of four available spots. He'll play Port Royal as an amateur. He's already won the 2026 WPGA Mid-Amateur Championship and a Minor League Golf Tour event earlier this month.

He's not a professional. He's not a household name. But he earned his spot in a 120-player PGA Tour field on pure performance, one round at a time.

That's the whole story, really.
